methodTitle:
A small calculation.
A clearer decision.
steps: Take the purchase price, add maintenance or financing costs, and subtract what you expect to resell it for.
Estimate how often you will use it and how long you will keep it. Give yourself room to be realistic.
Divide the net cost by expected uses. Try a lower-use scenario, or set a cost-per-use target that works for you.
extensionTag: A SECOND THOUGHT, ONE CLICK AWAY
extensionTitle:
Take the calculator
shopping with you.
extensionText: Open Cost Per Use right on a product page. Optional autofill reads the product details, so you can spend less time entering numbers and more time thinking about the purchase.
extensionNote: For Chrome on desktop. The calculator above works on your phone, too.
faqs: It is the net cost of a purchase divided by the number of times you expect to use it. A $200 purchase used 400 times costs $0.50 per use.
Does a low cost per use mean I should buy it?
Not necessarily. It is one way to compare purchases, not a measure of everything that matters. Consider your budget, your needs, and whether you already own something that does the job.

This website calculates in your browser and does not save or send your calculator inputs. The extension can save calculations locally in your browser. Our site host processes normal requests needed to serve the website.
Do I need to install anything?
No. Use this calculator here, on desktop or mobile. The free Chrome extension adds product-page autofill, comparison and local history.
